milestones.name: ATC Flight Plan Activated
rules: The Airport CDM Platform is initiated for this flight, and all available information is processed.
The flight plan may be used to update certain information such as type of aircraft.
For non coordinated airports, the flight plan is used to initiate the outbound flight.
The flight is ready not later than 15 minutes after the planned EOBT.

The system checks consistency between ATC Flight Plan, Airport Slot and Airport flight data and then confirms the flight to the Network Operations and allows further local processing of the flight, before the first E-DPI is sent.
The AO must provide correct information before the first E-DPI message, to feed Network Operations with consistent SOBT, aircraft registration, and first destination data, as early as possible.
The E-DPI message should not be sent if no or inconsistent information is provided.
This process is triggered by the first activation of the ATC Flight Plan (earliest EOBT-3 hr), or by new or late submissions of the ATC Flight Plan, after cancellation or revised EOBT.
ELDT and EIBT are updated for an arrival and EOBT and ETOT are updated for a departure.
The DPI process commences the correct messaging with Network Operations (if implemented).

milestones.name: EOBT - 2 hr
rules: If the flight is regulated, a CTOT is issued by Network Operations at EOBT-2h.
For inbound flights, ELDT is updated based on information provided by the FUM messages, taking into account the actual progress of the flight.
The system checks whether AO/GH flight estimates are consistent with the ATC Flight Plan, before or after take off from outstation.
At EOBT-2 hrs Network Operations is informed through the first T-DPI message of the updated take off time estimate.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT, if later than EOBT+EXOT.
In the case of manual input of TOBT, this estimate will override the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.
This procedure is triggered by a time stamp, at EOBT-2h.
ETOT/TTOT/CTOT are updated and appropriate fields are marked as REGULATED.

milestones.name: Take Off from Outstation
rules: The outstation provides ATOT to Network Operations and Aircraft Operator.
If the departure airport is more than 3hrs flying time from the destination, the ATOT is received and an ELDT is calculated using the Estimated Elapsed Time on the FPL.
If the flight is within 3hrs flying time of the destination, Network Operations monitors progress using ETFMS and sends a FUM providing updates of the flight's progress.

The system checks whether the AO/GH estimated landing time after take off from outstation are consistent with the outbound ATC Flight Plan, and when needed informs Network Operations about the updated take off time estimates using a T-DPI-t Message.
A TTOT tolerance of 5 minutes is respected before Network Operations is informed of the updated TTOT.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT.
In case EOBT is later than EIBT+MTTT, TTOT equals EOBT+EXOT.
In the case where TOBT is available this prediction will overrule the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.
This process is triggered by the take off from outstation.
ELDT, EIBT, TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: Local Radar Update
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code when the flight crosses a defined FIR/ATC boundary.
Update of the ELDT can trigger a new TOBT to be entered by the AO/GH, or calculated automatically by the Airport CDM Platform.
Any change to a stand or gate is not preferred after ELDT-30', taking into account the taxi-in time (EXIT).
An estimated in-block time (EIBT) is computed using the ELDT and the estimated taxi-in time.
The system commences the TOBT process and checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
The TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by the detection of the flight by radar in either FIR, TMA, or on Final Approach.
ELDT, EIBT, TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: Final Approach
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code and identifies when the flight crosses either a defined range/position or passes/leaves a predetermined level.
Update of the ELDT is used to determine a new TOBT.
The system commences the TOBT process and checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
The TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by the detection of the flight by radar in either FIR, TMA, or on Final Approach.
ELDT, EIBT, TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: Landed
rules: ALDT is provided by the ATC system or by ACARS from equipped aircraft (ACARS=ON), equivalent to ATC ATA.

The occurrence of ALDT triggers an update of downstream estimates: TOBT and TTOT are updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the defined turn-round period for the departing flight.
The EIBT can be updated according to the ALDT+EXIT.
The system checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by Actual Landing Time: ALDT.
ELDT changes to ALDT, and EIBT, TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: In-Block
rules: AIBT is provided by ACARS equipped aircraft or automated docking systems or ATC systems or by manual input (ACARS=IN), equivalent to Airline/Handler ATA.
ACGT is considered to commence at AIBT.

The occurrence of AIBT should trigger an update of downstream estimates: TOBT and TTOT are updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
The system checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by Actual In Blocks Time: AIBT.
EIBT changes to AIBT, TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: Ground Handling Started
rules: The occurrence of ACGT triggers an update of downstream estimates: TOBT is updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
The system checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by Actual Commence of Ground Handling: ACGT.
ETTT/TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: Final Confirmation of the TOBT
rules: The Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler provides the final TOBT t minutes before EOBT (t is a parameter time agreed locally).
The ATC system will calculate and provide the Estimated Taxi-Out Time (EXOT) based on the predicted traffic load, gate/stand location, runway in use, and waiting period at the Holding Position.
The flight is introduced into the pre-departure sequence following receipt of TOBT.
The system checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check should be performed at a predefined time (local parameter) to confirm TOBT prior to TSAT issue and verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan estimates given the updated TOBT.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.

This Milestone Process is constantly applicable in the CDM Platform, as soon as a TOBT is available; the confirmed TOBT prior to TSAT has special status, where AO/GH check the quality of TOBT before TSAT issue.
This process is triggered by a new TOBT or TTOT update; no need to confirm an existing TOBT if it has been manually modified before.

milestones.name: TSAT Issued
rules: ATC issues TSAT t-minutes before EOBT, where t is a parameter agreed locally.
The system informs all relevant partners of the TSAT that has been allocated to the flight.
Network Operations is informed by a T-DPI-s for non regulated flights; no check is performed for this step.
The system checks whether the number of TOBT updates exceeds a tolerance defined locally, after TSAT has been issued.
In case the number of TOBT updates exceeds a threshold, then the TOBT input should be processed according to local procedure.
This process is triggered by a defined time (local parameter) before TOBT, or by a TOBT update after TSAT issue.
TTOT is updated.

milestones.name: Boarding Starts
rules: The system informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Start Boarding Time (ASBT) when it occurs.
At a certain time before TOBT (local variable e.g. corresponding to aircraft type) a check shall be performed to check the boarding status and inform the AO/GH in case TOBT needs to be updated.
This process is triggered by a time variable <value> minutes before TOBT.

milestones.name: Aircraft Ready
rules: The system informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Ready Time (ARDT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft is ready for start up/push-back.
The system informs the AO/GH that TOBT has passed and the Airport CDM Platform has not yet received ARDT or Ready Status (RDY).
At TOBT + tolerance the AO/GH are informed that TOBT has passed and there has not been a ready status message yet.
ATC refines the pre-departure sequence.
The pilot requests start up just before TSAT, following coordination with the Ground Handler.
This procedure is triggered by an input to the Airport CDM Platform.

milestones.name: Start Up Requested
rules: The system informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Start up Request Time (ASRT) in the Airport CDM Platform when it occurs.
ATC confirms TSAT to the pilot in order to maintain the aircraft in the pre-departure sequence.
If the start up request is not made by TSAT + tolerance, the system alerts all relevant Airport CDM Partners that no start up has been requested, and the AO/GH should update TOBT.
The system timestamps when the tolerance window has passed at TSAT.

milestones.name: Start Up Approved
rules: ATC informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual start up approval Time (ASAT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has received start up approval/push-back clearance, when it occurs.
The system checks if ASAT is in accordance with TSAT and alerts all relevant Airport CDM Partners when no start up has been granted.
In case the start up approval is not granted at TSAT + tolerance, all relevant partners should be informed and the flight will be re-sequenced.
This is triggered by start up request by flight crew (voice or DCL) or a locally defined time around TSAT if Milestone Process 13 is omitted.

milestones.name: Off-Block
rules: The system informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Off-Block Time (AOBT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has commenced push-back/taxi from parking position, when it occurs.
TTOT is updated considering the EXOT.
AOBT always triggers an A-DPI message to Network Operations or, in the case of remote holding, at a defined time prior to TTOT.
After a first A-DPI is sent, the system checks TTOT updates against the TTOT tolerance before Network Operations is informed, with a new A-DPI, of the updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by AOBT detection.

milestones.name: Take Off
rules: ATOT is provided by ATC system or from ACARS equipped aircraft (ACARS=OFF), equivalent to ATC ATD.
FSA and MVT messages are sent.
The system informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners about the actual take off.
An airborne message is generated and the flight is removed from the departure sequence.
This process is triggered by Tower FDPS, A-SMGCS/Radar detection or ACARS.
